name: Affective Gating of Memory Circuit
short_description: Uses emotional intensity and novelty signals to gate memory consolidation, enhancing storage for emotionally salient or surprising events (flashbulb memory).

components.name: EMOTION_GATE
components.description: Opens memory consolidation gate based on emotional intensity of event

components.name: ENCODING_STATE_MONITOR
components.description: Assesses readiness and capacity of memory encoding systems

components.name: NOVELTY_AMPLIFIER
components.description: Amplifies consolidation signal for novel or surprising events

components.name: CONSOLIDATION_CONTROLLER
components.description: Integrates emotion, novelty, and encoding signals to control consolidation strength and flashbulb memory formation

key_references: McGaugh, J. L. (2004). The amygdala modulates the consolidation of memories of emotionally arousing experiences. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 27, 1–28.
LaBar, K. S., & Cabeza, R. (2006). Cognitive neuroscience of emotional memory. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 7(1), 54–64.
design_implications: Emotionally salient experiences are better remembered; use emotional resonance and novelty in museum, educational, or wayfinding designs where memorability is valued

Traumatic or intensely negative emotions can create vivid but distorted flashbulb memories; design threat-reducing contexts in high-stress environments (medical, security) to prevent false or intrusive memories
